marta: Quick heads-up — during the quarterly access sweep I spotted a KMS key with a very broad principal on the key policy (cross-account wildcard). Not sure when that happened. Can someone help triage? :grimacing:
jonah: Can you paste the policy snippet?
marta: Here — removed actual ARNs but kept structure:
```
{
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"*"},"Action":"kms:Encrypt","Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```
kevin: Oof. That looks like an accidental copy/paste of a template. If Principal is `*` it's effectively public for that action. Need to know: (1) which key id, (2) whether any grants were created, (3) CloudTrail events for kms:Encrypt/GenerateDataKey around the last 30d.
sasha: I can run the CloudTrail query and a quick list of grants. Suggest commands: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <KEY_ID> --query Policy` and `aws kms list-grants --key-id <KEY_ID>` — also `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GenerateDataKey` filtered by ResourceName.
jonah: If anyone needs an immediate mitigation, rotate key policy to a deny for external principals and put a temp tag `entitlement:investigate` so automation picks it up. Example patch: `aws kms put-key-policy --key-id <KEY_ID> --policy file://deny-external.json` (small canary patch).
marta: Key id is `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01`. No grants returned from `list-grants` when I ran it 10m ago.
kevin: Good. Still need to validate usage — list CloudTrail events and also check any S3 buckets or EBS volumes referencing the key. If it's unused we can quarantine and reissue.
sasha: CloudTrail shows two GenerateDataKey events 42 days ago but those are from our analytics account (111122223333). Both succeeded. No external account principals seen in the event source.
jonah: Ok so the policy was likely broadened but used only by internal account principals. Still a risk. Next steps: (A) patch policy to scoped principals, (B) create a JIRA `SEC-` ticket for entitlement cleanup, (C) run an automated scan across all keys for any principal wildcards, (D) update our access-review checklist to include KMS policy lint.
marta: I can own (A) and (B) — will create ticket and link it here.
kevin: I'll own (C) — quick script: `python scripts/kms_key_scan.py --lint wildcard_principal` and output CSV. If we find >5 keys with `*` we need a prioritized remediation window.
sasha: Also suggest adding an audit rule to the infra-policy repo that fails CI if `Principal: "*"` appears in a KMS policy file. We already lint IAM; KMS slipped through.
jonah: Agree. Also want us to verify retention of KMS CloudTrail logs for at least 90d for forensic reasons. Audit-bot, can you create a retention alert if any KMS-related trail < 90d?
audit-bot: Alert created: `kms-cloudtrail-retention-check`. Will post weekly digest to #eng-security.
marta: Putting initial remediation ETA end of day tomorrow. Will apply a conservative scoped policy that matches service principals and the analytics account, then rotate usage keys if needed.
kevin: After patch, we should run a canary access test and capture `kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey` traces to ensure nothing broken. Rollback plan: reapply previous policy from snapshot if any production failure.
sasha: Adding a short howto in the ticket for oncall to follow if something breaks: run `aws kms simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <arn> --action-names kms:Encrypt` against service principals.
jonah: One follow-up: let's add a small metric to Console showing KMS keys with external principals as a risky-flag. Helps product ops catch drifts.
marta: Agree. Ticket created: SEC-4821 — I added the policy diff, CloudTrail snippets, and assigned kevin for scan.
kevin: Scan kickoff scheduled in 30m. Will share CSV in the ticket.
sasha: Nice catch. Also we should mark this as part of the Q-access-review retro so process changes stick. :thumbsup:
jonah: Thanks everyone. If anything suspicious shows up from the scan, escalate to incident channel `#incidents` and set Sev 2 until mitigated.
marta: Closing the thread for now; will post updates in the ticket and ping here when the policy patch is live. Thanks! :heart:
